Probably not with normal unaided eyesight.

Although the Moon is high above the horizon and the sky is clear, it is an extremely thin crescent—only **2.74% illuminated**—and just **19° from the Sun**. In bright midday sky, that gives it very low contrast. Its relatively favorable altitude and your knowing where to look help, but an ordinary observer would still be unlikely to detect it reliably.

**Practical verdict:** possible under exceptional conditions and with very precise positioning, but **unlikely naked-eye**. Binoculars could make it easier, but using them this close to the Sun is hazardous—only attempt it if the Sun is completely blocked by a solid object and there is no possibility of sweeping across it.
